The JSON block below is the enforceable rule contract. Edit both prose and JSON when changing policy.

evidence.source_quote:
One of the major dangers of calling external contracts is that they can take over the control flow. In the reentrancy attack (a.k.a. recursive call attack), a malicious contract calls back into the calling contract before the first invocation of the function is finished. This may cause the different invocations of the function to interact in undesirable ways.

## Remediation

The best practices to avoid Reentrancy weaknesses are:

- Make sure all internal state changes are performed before the call is executed. This is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern
- Use a reentrancy lock (ie. OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard).
evidence.scope: Legacy SWC guidance; check compiler and EVM applicability

tweets: Calling external contracts can transfer control before your function finishes, allowing another contract to execute first.
This allows a malicious contract to call back into you before the original invocation completes.
Different invocations of the same function may then interact in undesirable ways.
To avoid this, perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
